metadata.label: Title
metadata.value: Glass Plate negative collection: Arnold Fairbairns for Stephen Warner’s book Lincoln College, Oxford

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Glass plate negatives from the original photography commissioned by Stephen A. Warner from 'his old college friend' Arnold Fairbairns. They were used extensively to illustrate Warner's history of Lincoln College, published in 1908. In the preface Warner acknowledges Fairbairns' 'magnificent series of photographs'. They appear to have been undertaken as a fairly systematic survey of College and include exterior and interior views, Rectors' signatures from documents in the archives, plate, portraits, memorials and views of College property.

metadata.value: Descriptions prepared by Jon Newman c.2000, Lindsay McCormack and John Jeffs, 2019.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Chapel plate. Silver flat-topped Communion Flagon with cover, engraved with arms and a presentation inscription of Sir Edmund Denton \[Alexander Denton?\] of Hilsdon, Bucks. Maker's mark TK a four leaf clover below, London, 1671, cylindrical body engraved with the arms of the donor and an inscription dated 1672, spreading skirt base, flattened domed cover engraved with the College arms, pierced thumbpiece and scroll handle, scratch weight 60oz 5d, 12Â¾in high, engraved weight is 70oz.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: College plate. Silver jug; inscription and arms of donor, Thomas Bathurst, son of Benjamin Bathurst, of Lidney, Glos. R Gurney & T Cooke, London, 1743, plain baluster body on spreading foot with pronounced everted lip spout, scroll handle, engraved with the arms of the College and the donor, 9in high, 37oz.

metadata.label: Description

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: College plate. Two-handled cup engraved with the arms of College, a presentation inscription and the arms of the donor. Silver. London, 1762. Maker T C W W in a circle. metadata.label: Description

(gu.) of Nocton, Lincolnshire on a fess (arg.) between three crescents (or) as many escallopes (az.) with the Ulster Badge.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: College plate. A Queen Anne silver tankard with cover engraved with the arms of College and a presentation inscription and the arms of Nicholas Corsellis. Robert Timbrell, London, 1702, slightly tapering cylindrical body engraved with the arms of Corsellis de Wivenhoe and with an inscription, the flat domed cover with the arms of the college, scroll handle with knurled thumbpiece, 8Â½in high, 40.8oz, some repairs.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Chapel plate. A Charles II silver altar candlestick. One of a pair of candlesticks, maker's mark DB an annulet below, London, 1683, the large square bases rising to similarly shaped flanges below fluted column stems, engraved with a presentation inscription from Georgius Wheler \[George Wheler\] dated 1683, also with scratch weights 23 11 and 23 7, fitted with later pricket sockets, John Swift, London, circa 1750, 10Â½in high, the bases 6Â¾in square.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: College plate. A George III oval basket engraved with the arms of College and the donor. Silver. London, 1763 or 1765. Maker illegible. Height, 4.5 inches, diameter 15.75 by 13.125 inches. Arms of donor, Nicholas Corsellis, of Wivenhoe, Essex (az.) a griffin sergeant (or), quartered with those of Child, of Woodford (vert) two bars engrailed between three leopards' heads (or).

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: College plate. A silver jug with lid. Edward Pocock, London, circa 1723, with hinged lid surmounted by a baluster finial and engraved \'Coll Linc\', the baluster body on spreading foot, applied with a girdle and short spout, scroll handle, engraved with the College arms and those of the donor, presentation inscription of Henry Hamilton dated 1735, scratch weight 55:8, 12in high, 57.5oz. Makers mark stamped twice, date letter H for 1723, cover unmarked.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Chapel plate. A Charles I silver Communion Cup and Paten Cover, maker's mark TH a device (perhaps an escallop shell) below, London, 1625, the plain cup on stepped circular base with stamped ovolo border, similar decoration to the knop, the beaker shaped bowl everted at the lip, the paten with reeded rim and spool shaped knop, scratch weights respectively 11oz 17d and 3oz 3d, 7Â¾in high, paten 4in diameter.
